records.text: TMATH 109 Financial and Mathematical Foundations (5) RSN Interprets everyday financial events using quantitative and algebraic reasoning and models. records.text: TMATH 316 Financial Mathematics (5) RSN Introduces students to fundamental concepts in financial mathematics: compound and simple interest, nominal and effective rates, present and future value, discount rates, force of interest. records.header: TMATH 413 Coding Theory (5) RSN
records.text: TMATH 413 Coding Theory (5) RSN Deals with electronic communication over noisy channels where some bits of information may get corrupted. Covers using codes in designing ciphers secure in the era of quantum computers. Topics include error-detection/correction, various types of codes, and McEliece cipher. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in either TMATH 208 or TCSS 321.

records.title: History of Mathematics
records.header: TMATH 420 History of Mathematics (5) SSc, RSN
records.text: TMATH 420 History of Mathematics (5) SSc, RSN Surveys the history and development of mathematics from its earliest beginnings into the early twentieth century. Focuses on the effect math discovery and literacy has had on human, social, and cultural behaviors. Course overlaps with: STMATH 420. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in either TMATH 126, TMATH 207, TMATH 208, or TMATH 300.

records.title: Introduction to Real Analysis I
records.header: TMATH 424 Introduction to Real Analysis I (5) NSc, RSN
records.text: TMATH 424 Introduction to Real Analysis I (5) NSc, RSN Introduces set theory; the construction of the real numbers; infima and suprema; metric spaces and Euclidean distance; topology of the reals numbers; formal treatment of limits; Cauchy sequences; continuity; uniform convergence; and the derivative. Course overlaps with: MATH 327 and STMATH 424. Prerequisite: minimum grade of 2.0 in TMATH 300.

records.title: Introduction to Real Analysis II
records.header: TMATH 425 Introduction to Real Analysis II (5) RSN
records.text: TMATH 425 Introduction to Real Analysis II (5) RSN Provides rigorous treatment of the derivative of a function of one variable; Contraction Mapping Theorem; Riemann integral, Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Cauchy existence criterion; sequences of functions, pointwise and uniform convergence; power series; differentiation of functions on Euclidean spaces, total derivative; and Implicit Function Theorem. Course overlaps with: MATH 328 and STMATH 425. Prerequisite: minimum grade of 2.0 in TMATH 424.

records.title: Complex Analysis
records.header: TMATH 427 Complex Analysis (5) RSN
records.text: TMATH 427 Complex Analysis (5) RSN Introduces concept of Complex numbers; Power series and Complex functions; Mobius transformations; Riemann sphere; Cauchy-Riemann equations; Complex differentiation and integration; Residue theorem; Cauchy integral formula; Conformal mapping. Course overlaps with: MATH 427 and STMATH 427. Prerequisite: Minimum grade of 2.0 in TMATH 300 or TMATH 324.

records.title: Math, Power, and Society
records.header: TMATH 473 Math, Power, and Society (5) DIV
records.text: TMATH 473 Math, Power, and Society (5) DIV Critically examines mathematics education through lenses of identity, power and diversity in the US context. Special attention focuses on mathematics education as a tool of institutional oppression and liberation based on race, gender, class, and language; and how we can make mathematics more accessible, engaging, and transformative. Course equivalent to: T EDUC 473.
